description: No-store keyset counter for the relations the full mirror sync cannot finish (each hit max_rows_per_relation=1,000,000 with 0 committed on 2026-10-01) and the one that returned HTTP 500: per relation the true row and distinct-key count from a key-columns-only traversal, and id stability (the first 20,000 keys read twice in the run; ratio of first-read ids the second read saw; 16-hex key-list hashes for comparison with the previous run). classification says which defect it is: data_truth_defect (ids change between reads: an upstream ETL re-inserting rows under fresh ids; report upstream), paging_defect (a key recurs on a later page), mirror_bound (stable ids, the true count exceeds the mirror bound), upstream_unavailable (HTTP failure after halving the page down to 250), inconclusive or ok. For a relation whose natural key integrations.source_mirror derives (an owned child row: Portal ETL and receipt upserts re-insert such rows under fresh ids), both reads also carry the natural-key columns and replaced_rows / ambiguous_replacements count first-read keys gone by the second read whose natural key a new key carries (one to one in both reads, else ambiguous); counts over the samples only, a lower bound. The relations rotate across daily runs (each with the whole remaining budget, least recently completed first): complete_count counts the relations completed by this run or by one at most rotation_window_hours (96) ago, whose run relations[*].completed_at names; complete_this_run_count is this run alone, and a relation this run cut stays count_lower_bound (inconclusive). A relation one run's 3300 s budget cannot hold runs to the 6400 s daily deadline; one cut even then is named in exceeds_daily_bound and never counts complete. Output is counts, booleans, hashes, run stamps and relation names only; row_data_check.leaked proves no key or value is printed.
notes: live-unverified until a live-check result exists. Measurement only: GET /v1/relations once, then keyset pages of the key columns through integrations.workbench_read_api (no other HTTP path); an 8-byte digest per key lives in memory for the distinct count and nothing is written. Rotation, decided by measurement (2026-10-11): the 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-11 daily runs read 10.2-11.5k keys/s per relation at page 5000 (the service maximum, workbench-api query.mjs LIMITS.maxLimit) with 0 throttle waits, and the four ETL-grown relations stopped on budget at 2.95-3.47M keys after ~300 s each; from their silver sources (2026-09-30: 15,137 statuses, 20,825 production tasks, 63,659 assembly order items) times the ~428 copies app_assembly_order_damage holds (2,572,222 / 6,012), app_manufacturing_order_line alone is about 27M keys, about 2,500 s on its own keyset traversal (sequential by nature, so parallel relations do not shorten it), and all six about 50M keys. So no run fits every relation; each run gives the relations, least recently completed first, the whole remaining budget (3300 s: one relation up to about 32M keys), a relation whose last traversal needed more than is left is not reached (stop rotation, verdict not_reached, nothing read), and the first relation of a run that was cut yields the first turn once. Daily deadline (rotation accepted, no durable cursor): a relation the previous report shows one run cannot hold (cut by the budget with the first turn, or need_seconds over 3300) gets --daily-budget-seconds 6400 instead (relations[*].budget_extended); the others keep 3300 s. One the budget cuts with the first turn and the whole 6400 s is exceeds_daily_bound (named in exceeds_daily_bound until a run completes it) and stays count_lower_bound: never complete, so complete_count stays under 6 and the check fails, red and honest, never a stitched count. The exceeds_daily_bound names and then relations[*].budget_extended are recorded last: the recorded detail is capped at 4000 characters (verify/live_verify.py MAX_DETAIL_CHARS; the 2026-10-13 run recorded 3866), so an over-long detail (a carried previous report adds previous_report_carried) drops them, budget_extended first, before the relations[*] rotation fields. Timeout 7000 s means a run that needs it takes most of one daily command (the runner's starved-spec rule runs it first in one). Timeout 7000 s keeps 600 s over the 6400 s deadline (a page's throttle retries alone can wait 5 x 60 s) and stays under the runtime's 7200 s command limit with the runner's kill grace (verify/live_verify.py COMMAND_LIMIT_SECONDS). A relation unserved or unreadable this run is never rotated out and never counts complete (upstream_unavailable). A not-reached relation carries its streaks, so the two-run rule counts measured runs. Rotation memory lives only in the previous daily report's fields: a blocked or timed-out run records none, so the runner (carry_previous_measured) then passes the newest daily report whose mirror.relation_counts check recorded fields, up to 96 h old (verify/live_verify.py measured_previous; the check records its checked_at as previous_report_carried), and the next run keeps rotation_rank, need_seconds and completed_at. A traversal is never resumed across runs: the service cursor is base64url JSON of the last key's values, which this output never carries (row_data_check) and the runner would reduce to its length or redact. Distinct keys are 8-byte digests in one flat array (about 18 MB per million keys; 40M keys about 512 MB) for the cross-page repeat test. A relation cut by the budget or --max-keys is count_lower_bound (inconclusive). --previous-report={daily_report} is the runner's --daily-report (results/daily/latest.json): previous_run_hash_equal compares first_keys_hash with it, and defect_streak/stable_streak carry the two-run rule (data_truth_defect on two consecutive daily runs -> unstable_relations, which mirror.full_coverage reads key-only and drops from the completeness denominator; two consecutive conclusive stable runs clear it). Without a daily report the streaks start from this run. The check fails on a NEW data-truth defect (new_data_truth_defect_count: classified data_truth_defect and not already in the previous daily report's unstable_relations) or an unreadable relation, so a finding is reported once; known unstable relations are reported (unstable_relations, relations[*].defect_streak/stable_streak/unstable) without failing every day. A previous daily report more than 36 h old (previous_report_age_hours) does not continue a streak (previous_report_consecutive false). When results/daily/latest.json is absent the runner passes the newest complete daily set beside the --merge-into file instead, so the streaks keep their previous run (verify/live_verify.py previous_daily).
